The form now saves the BMI value as a persisted obs, but I could not find the server-side change or the ticket that introduced it.

**What the form stores.** The browser still calculates BMI from weight and height (rounded to one decimal). On save, the form writes a `bodyMassIndex` obs (concept `bodyMassIndexUuid`) with that value into the vitals encounter. When creating, it adds the obs whenever a BMI was computed. When editing, it adds a new obs and voids the previous one, but only if weight or height changed. Once the obs is persisted, the listing reads the BMI's own `bmi` value and interpretation back from the server (`openmrs-esm-patient-chart/packages/esm-patient-vitals-app/src/common/data.resource.ts:309-335`, `:362-366`). Interpretation is only shown when the server returns it for the persisted obs. I did not confirm the server-side code that assigns BMI interpretation against the concept's reference ranges. The FHIR translator I found (`openmrs-module-fhir2/.../ObservationInterpretationTranslatorImpl.java`) maps interpretations in the other direction, from FHIR to OpenMRS.

**How older encounters show a value.** Encounters with no persisted BMI obs fall back to the client-side calculation from their stored weight and height (`data.resource.ts:362-366`). They display a number but get no interpretation flag, so they are never flagged low or high.

**The change and ticket.** I did not find a commit or a ticket that explicitly introduced this. The only ticket reference I found is O3-4825, in `openmrs-esm-patient-chart/e2e/specs/age-based-vitals.spec.ts:38`. It concerns preschooler age-specific ranges for pulse, respiratory rate and blood pressure, not BMI. My Falkon tools cannot search commit history, so a commit lookup needs `git log -S bodyMassIndex` on the chart repo or a search of the fhir2 and core histories.
